(* Float's operators and functions bound to nativeHelpers keep their values under walk, at zeros, large values, the infinities and NaN. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk
export Executable

run():() = do
  z: RR64 = asFloat(0.0)
  nz: RR64 = -z
  one: RR64 = asFloat(1.0)
  two: RR64 = asFloat(2.0)
  a: RR64 = asFloat(2.5)
  b: RR64 = asFloat(-0.75)
  large: RR64 = asFloat(1000000000000000000000.0)
  huge: RR64 = (large DOT large) DOT (large DOT large)
  inf: RR64 = (huge DOT huge) DOT (huge DOT huge)
  ninf: RR64 = -inf
  nan: RR64 = z / z
  m1: RR64 = asFloat(-1.0)
  half: RR64 = asFloat(0.5)
  four: RR64 = asFloat(4.0)
  sq: RR64 = asFloat(6.25)
  nlarge: RR64 = -large

  assert(a.asString, "2.5", "asString")
  assert(asFloat(0.1).asString, "0.1", "asString of 0.1")
  assert(large.asString, "1.0E21", "asString of a large value")
  assert(z.asString, "0.0", "asString of 0.0")
  assert(nz.asString, "-0.0", "asString of -0.0")
  assert(huge.asString, "1.0E84", "asString of 1.0E84")
  assert(inf.asString, "Infinity", "asString of infinity, from an overflow")
  assert(ninf.asString, "-Infinity", "asString of -infinity")
  assert(nan.asString, "NaN", "asString of NaN")
  assert(b.asExprString, "-0.75", "asExprString")
  assert(nz.asExprString, "-0.0", "asExprString of -0.0")
  assert(z.asExprString, "0.0", "asExprString of 0.0")
  assert(large.asExprString, "1.0E21", "asExprString of a large value")
  assert(inf.asExprString, "Infinity", "asExprString of infinity")
  assert(ninf.asExprString, "-Infinity", "asExprString of -infinity")
  assert(nan.asExprString, "NaN", "asExprString of NaN")

  assert(|a|, 2.5, "|a|")
  assert(|b|, 0.75, "|b|")
  assert((|z|).asString, "0.0", "|0.0|")
  assert(|inf|, inf, "|infinity|")
  assert((|nz|).asString, "0.0", "|-0.0|")
  assert(|ninf|, inf, "|-infinity|")
  assert((|nan|).isNaN, true, "|NaN|")
  assert(|large|, large, "|large|")
  assert(|nlarge|, large, "|-large|")

  assert(a = a, true, "=")
  assert(a = b, false, "= unequal")
  assert(z = nz, true, "0.0 = -0.0")
  assert(inf = inf, true, "infinity = infinity")
  assert(inf = large, false, "infinity = large")
  assert(large = large, true, "large = large")
  assert(ninf = ninf, true, "-infinity = -infinity")
  assert(ninf = inf, false, "-infinity = infinity")
  assert(b < a, true, "<")
  assert(a < b, false, "< not")
  assert(nz < z, false, "-0.0 < 0.0")
  assert(large < inf, true, "large < infinity")
  assert(ninf < b, true, "-infinity < b")
  assert(b <= a, true, "<=")
  assert(a <= a, true, "<= equal")
  assert(a <= b, false, "<= not")
  assert(z <= nz, true, "0.0 <= -0.0")
  assert(inf <= inf, true, "infinity <= infinity")
  assert(large <= inf, true, "large <= infinity")
  assert(ninf <= nz, true, "-infinity <= -0.0")
  assert(a > b, true, ">")
  assert(b > a, false, "> not")
  assert(z > nz, false, "0.0 > -0.0")
  assert(inf > large, true, "infinity > large")
  assert(large > a, true, "large > a")
  assert(ninf > large, false, "-infinity > large")
  assert(inf > ninf, true, "infinity > -infinity")
  assert(a >= b, true, ">=")
  assert(b >= b, true, ">= equal")
  assert(b >= a, false, ">= not")
  assert(nz >= z, true, "-0.0 >= 0.0")
  assert(ninf >= ninf, true, "-infinity >= -infinity")
  assert(z >= nz, true, "0.0 >= -0.0")
  assert(large >= large, true, ">= of large values")
  assert(inf >= ninf, true, "infinity >= -infinity")

  assert(-a, -2.5, "unary -")
  assert((-b), 0.75, "unary - of a negative")
  assert((-z).asString, "-0.0", "unary - of 0.0")
  assert((-nz).asString, "0.0", "unary - of -0.0")
  assert(-inf, ninf, "unary - of infinity")
  assert((-large).asString, "-1.0E21", "unary - of a large value")
  assert(-ninf, inf, "unary - of -infinity")
  assert((-nan).isNaN, true, "unary - of NaN")

  assert(a + b, 1.75, "+")
  assert((z + nz).asString, "0.0", "0.0 + -0.0")
  assert((nz + nz).asString, "-0.0", "-0.0 + -0.0")
  assert((large + large).asString, "2.0E21", "+ of large values")
  assert(inf + one, inf, "infinity + 1")
  assert((inf + ninf).isNaN, true, "infinity + -infinity")
  assert((nan + one).isNaN, true, "NaN + 1")
  assert(a - b, 3.25, "-")
  assert((z - z).asString, "0.0", "0.0 - 0.0")
  assert((nz - z).asString, "-0.0", "-0.0 - 0.0")
  assert(ninf - large, ninf, "-infinity - large")
  assert((inf - inf).isNaN, true, "infinity - infinity")
  assert((nan - one).isNaN, true, "NaN - 1")
  assert(a DOT b, -1.875, "DOT")
  assert((large DOT large).asString, "1.0E42", "DOT of large values")
  assert((nz DOT a).asString, "-0.0", "-0.0 DOT 2.5")
  assert((inf DOT z).isNaN, true, "infinity DOT 0.0")
  assert((nz DOT nz).asString, "0.0", "-0.0 DOT -0.0")
  assert(ninf DOT b, inf, "-infinity DOT b")
  assert((nan DOT one).isNaN, true, "NaN DOT 1")
  assert(a TIMES a, 6.25, "TIMES")
  assert(inf TIMES b, ninf, "infinity TIMES b")
  assert((z TIMES b).asString, "-0.0", "0.0 TIMES b")
  assert((nan TIMES z).isNaN, true, "NaN TIMES 0.0")
  assert((nz TIMES nz).asString, "0.0", "-0.0 TIMES -0.0")
  assert((large TIMES large).asString, "1.0E42", "TIMES of large values")
  assert(ninf TIMES a, ninf, "-infinity TIMES a")
  assert(a b, -1.875, "juxtaposition")
  assert(ninf ninf, inf, "juxtaposition of -infinities")
  assert((b z).asString, "-0.0", "juxtaposition of b and 0.0")
  assert((nz a).asString, "-0.0", "juxtaposition of -0.0 and a")
  assert((large large).asString, "1.0E42", "juxtaposition of large values")
  assert(inf a, inf, "juxtaposition of infinity and a")
  assert((nan a).isNaN, true, "juxtaposition of NaN and a")
  assert(a / b, -3.3333333333333335, "/")
  assert((one / ninf).asString, "-0.0", "1 / -infinity")
  assert(large / large, one, "/ of large values")
  assert((inf / inf).isNaN, true, "infinity / infinity")
  assert(nan.isNaN, true, "0.0 / 0.0")
  assert((nz / a).asString, "-0.0", "-0.0 / a")
  assert(inf / a, inf, "infinity / a")
  assert(ninf / b, inf, "-infinity / b")
  assert((large / inf).asString, "0.0", "large / infinity")
  assert((nan / one).isNaN, true, "NaN / 1")
  assert(SQRT sq, 2.5, "SQRT")
  assert((SQRT nz).asString, "-0.0", "SQRT of -0.0")
  assert(SQRT inf, inf, "SQRT of infinity")
  assert((SQRT b).isNaN, true, "SQRT of a negative")
  assert((SQRT nan).isNaN, true, "SQRT of NaN")
  assert((SQRT z).asString, "0.0", "SQRT of 0.0")
  assert((SQRT large).asString, "3.1622776601683792E10", "SQRT of a large value")
  assert((SQRT ninf).isNaN, true, "SQRT of -infinity")

  assert(a^two, 6.25, "^ at a Float exponent")
  assert(two^m1, 0.5, "^ at a negative Float exponent")
  assert(z^nz, one, "0.0 ^ -0.0")
  assert(two^inf, inf, "2.0 ^ infinity")
  assert((b^half).isNaN, true, "^ of a negative at 0.5")
  assert((large^two).asString, "1.0E42", "^ of a large value at 2.0")
  assert(ninf^two, inf, "-infinity ^ 2.0")
  assert((inf^m1).asString, "0.0", "infinity ^ -1.0")
  assert(nan^z, one, "NaN ^ 0.0")
  assert((two^nan).isNaN, true, "2.0 ^ NaN")
  assert(a^2.0, 6.25, "^ at an RR64 exponent")
  assert(four^0.5, two, "^ at 0.5")
  assert(large^0.0, one, "^ of a large value at 0.0")
  assert(ninf^3.0, ninf, "-infinity ^ 3.0")
  assert((z^2.0).asString, "0.0", "0.0 ^ 2.0")
  assert((nz^3.0).asString, "-0.0", "-0.0 ^ 3.0")
  assert(inf^0.5, inf, "infinity ^ 0.5")
  assert((nan^2.0).isNaN, true, "NaN ^ 2.0")

  assert(sin(z), z, "sin 0.0")
  assert(sin(nz).asString, "-0.0", "sin -0.0")
  assert(sin(asFloat(3.141592653589793)), 1.2246467991473532 TIMES 10.0^(-16), "sin pi")
  assert(sin(inf).isNaN, true, "sin infinity")
  assert(sin(nan).isNaN, true, "sin NaN")
  assert(sin(large), -0.6671201770718048, "sin of a large value")
  assert(sin(ninf).isNaN, true, "sin -infinity")
  assert(cos(z), one, "cos 0.0")
  assert(cos(nz), one, "cos -0.0")
  assert(cos(asFloat(3.141592653589793)), -one, "cos pi")
  assert(cos(ninf).isNaN, true, "cos -infinity")
  assert(cos(large), 0.7449501119831339, "cos of a large value")
  assert(cos(inf).isNaN, true, "cos infinity")
  assert(cos(nan).isNaN, true, "cos NaN")
  assert(tan(z), z, "tan 0.0")
  assert(tan(nz).asString, "-0.0", "tan -0.0")
  assert(tan(asFloat(0.7853981633974483)), 0.9999999999999999, "tan pi/4")
  assert(tan(inf).isNaN, true, "tan infinity")
  assert(tan(large), -0.8955232925542654, "tan of a large value")
  assert(tan(ninf).isNaN, true, "tan -infinity")
  assert(tan(nan).isNaN, true, "tan NaN")
  assert(asin(half), 0.5235987755982989, "asin 0.5")
  assert(asin(one), 1.5707963267948966, "asin 1")
  assert(asin(nz).asString, "-0.0", "asin -0.0")
  assert(asin(two).isNaN, true, "asin 2")
  assert(asin(z).asString, "0.0", "asin 0.0")
  assert(asin(large).isNaN, true, "asin of a large value")
  assert(asin(inf).isNaN, true, "asin infinity")
  assert(asin(ninf).isNaN, true, "asin -infinity")
  assert(asin(nan).isNaN, true, "asin NaN")
  assert(acos(half), 1.0471975511965979, "acos 0.5")
  assert(acos(one), z, "acos 1")
  assert(acos(two).isNaN, true, "acos 2")
  assert(acos(z), 1.5707963267948966, "acos 0.0")
  assert(acos(nz), 1.5707963267948966, "acos -0.0")
  assert(acos(large).isNaN, true, "acos of a large value")
  assert(acos(inf).isNaN, true, "acos infinity")
  assert(acos(ninf).isNaN, true, "acos -infinity")
  assert(acos(nan).isNaN, true, "acos NaN")
  assert(atan(one), 0.7853981633974483, "atan 1")
  assert(atan(nz).asString, "-0.0", "atan -0.0")
  assert(atan(inf), 1.5707963267948966, "atan infinity")
  assert(atan(ninf), -1.5707963267948966, "atan -infinity")
  assert(atan(nan).isNaN, true, "atan NaN")
  assert(atan(z).asString, "0.0", "atan 0.0")
  assert(atan(large), 1.5707963267948966, "atan of a large value")
  assert(log(asFloat(2.718281828459045)), one, "log e")
  assert(log(one), z, "log 1")
  assert(log(z), ninf, "log 0.0")
  assert(log(nz), ninf, "log -0.0")
  assert(log(inf), inf, "log infinity")
  assert(log(b).isNaN, true, "log of a negative")
  assert(log(large), 48.35428695287496, "log of a large value")
  assert(log(ninf).isNaN, true, "log -infinity")
  assert(log(nan).isNaN, true, "log NaN")
  assert(exp(one), 2.718281828459045, "exp 1")
  assert(exp(z), one, "exp 0.0")
  assert(exp(nz), one, "exp -0.0")
  assert(exp(ninf), z, "exp -infinity")
  assert(exp(inf), inf, "exp infinity")
  assert(exp(large), inf, "exp of a large value")
  assert(exp(nan).isNaN, true, "exp NaN")

  assert(floor(a), two, "floor")
  assert(floor(b), -one, "floor of a negative")
  assert(floor(nz).asString, "-0.0", "floor -0.0")
  assert(floor(large), large, "floor of a large value")
  assert(floor(z).asString, "0.0", "floor 0.0")
  assert(ceiling(a), asFloat(3.0), "ceiling")
  assert(ceiling(b).asString, "-0.0", "ceiling of -0.75")
  assert(ceiling(z).asString, "0.0", "ceiling 0.0")
  assert(ceiling(large), large, "ceiling of a large value")
  assert(ceiling(nz).asString, "-0.0", "ceiling -0.0")
  assert(truncate(a), 2, "truncate")
  assert(truncate(asFloat(-2.7)), -2, "truncate toward zero")
  assert(truncate(b), 0, "truncate of -0.75")
  assert(truncate(asFloat(4503599627370496.0)).asString, "4503599627370496", "truncate of 2^52")
  assert(truncate(z), 0, "truncate 0.0")
  assert(truncate(nz), 0, "truncate -0.0")
  assert(round(a), 2, "round half to even, down")
  assert(round(asFloat(3.5)), 4, "round half to even, up")
  assert(round(asFloat(-2.5)), -2, "round of a negative half")
  assert(round(asFloat(2.7)), 3, "round up")
  assert(round(b), -1, "round of -0.75")
  assert(round(asFloat(4503599627370496.0)).asString, "4503599627370496", "round of 2^52")
  assert(round(z), 0, "round 0.0")
  assert(round(nz), 0, "round -0.0")
end

component NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled
export Executable

  z: RR64 = 0.0
  nz: RR64 = dNeg(z)
  one: RR64 = 1.0
  two: RR64 = 2.0
  a: RR64 = 2.5
  b: RR64 = dNeg(0.75)
  large: RR64 = 1000000000000000000000.0
  huge: RR64 = dMul(dMul(large, large), dMul(large, large))
  inf: RR64 = dMul(dMul(huge, huge), dMul(huge, huge))
  ninf: RR64 = dNeg(inf)
  nan: RR64 = dDiv(z, z)

  assert(dToString(a) = "2.5", "dToString")
  assert(dToString(0.1) = "0.1", "dToString of 0.1")
  assert(dToString(large) = "1.0E21", "dToString of a large value")
  assert(dToString(z) = "0.0", "dToString of 0.0")
  assert(dToString(nz) = "-0.0", "dToString of -0.0")
  assert(dToString(huge) = "1.0E84", "dToString of 1.0E84")
  assert(dToString(inf) = "Infinity", "dToString of infinity, from an overflow")
  assert(dToString(ninf) = "-Infinity", "dToString of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(nan) = "NaN", "dToString of NaN")
  assert(dToString(b) = "-0.75", "dToString of -0.75")

  assert(dEQ(dAbs(a), a), "dAbs")
  assert(dEQ(dAbs(b), 0.75), "dAbs of a negative")
  assert(dToString(dAbs(z)) = "0.0", "dAbs of 0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dAbs(inf), inf), "dAbs of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dAbs(nz)) = "0.0", "dAbs of -0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dAbs(ninf), inf), "dAbs of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dAbs(nan)) = "NaN", "dAbs of NaN")
  assert(dEQ(dAbs(large), large), "dAbs of a large value")
  assert(dEQ(dAbs(dNeg(large)), large), "dAbs of -large")

  assert(dEQ(a, a), "dEQ")
  assert(NOT dEQ(a, b), "dEQ unequal")
  assert(dEQ(z, nz), "dEQ of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dEQ(inf, inf), "dEQ of infinities")
  assert(NOT dEQ(inf, large), "dEQ of infinity and a large value")
  assert(dEQ(large, large), "dEQ of large values")
  assert(dEQ(ninf, ninf), "dEQ of -infinities")
  assert(NOT dEQ(ninf, inf), "dEQ of -infinity and infinity")
  assert(dLT(b, a), "dLT")
  assert(NOT dLT(a, b), "dLT not")
  assert(NOT dLT(nz, z), "dLT of -0.0 and 0.0")
  assert(dLT(large, inf), "dLT of a large value and infinity")
  assert(dLT(ninf, b), "dLT of -infinity and b")
  assert(dLE(b, a), "dLE")
  assert(dLE(a, a), "dLE equal")
  assert(NOT dLE(a, b), "dLE not")
  assert(dLE(z, nz), "dLE of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dLE(inf, inf), "dLE of infinities")
  assert(dLE(large, inf), "dLE of a large value and infinity")
  assert(dLE(ninf, nz), "dLE of -infinity and -0.0")
  assert(dGT(a, b), "dGT")
  assert(NOT dGT(b, a), "dGT not")
  assert(NOT dGT(z, nz), "dGT of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dGT(inf, large), "dGT of infinity and a large value")
  assert(dGT(large, a), "dGT of a large value and a")
  assert(NOT dGT(ninf, large), "dGT of -infinity and a large value")
  assert(dGT(inf, ninf), "dGT of infinity and -infinity")
  assert(dGE(a, b), "dGE")
  assert(dGE(b, b), "dGE equal")
  assert(NOT dGE(b, a), "dGE not")
  assert(dGE(nz, z), "dGE of -0.0 and 0.0")
  assert(dGE(ninf, ninf), "dGE of -infinities")
  assert(dGE(z, nz), "dGE of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dGE(large, large), "dGE of large values")
  assert(dGE(inf, ninf), "dGE of infinity and -infinity")

  assert(dEQ(dNeg(a), dNeg(2.5)), "dNeg")
  assert(dEQ(dNeg(b), 0.75), "dNeg of a negative")
  assert(dToString(nz) = "-0.0", "dNeg of 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dNeg(nz)) = "0.0", "dNeg of -0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dNeg(inf), ninf), "dNeg of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dNeg(large)) = "-1.0E21", "dNeg of a large value")
  assert(dEQ(dNeg(ninf), inf), "dNeg of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dNeg(nan)) = "NaN", "dNeg of NaN")

  assert(dEQ(dAdd(a, b), 1.75), "dAdd")
  assert(dToString(dAdd(z, nz)) = "0.0", "dAdd of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dAdd(nz, nz)) = "-0.0", "dAdd of -0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dAdd(large, large)) = "2.0E21", "dAdd of large values")
  assert(dEQ(dAdd(inf, one), inf), "dAdd of infinity and 1")
  assert(dToString(dAdd(inf, ninf)) = "NaN", "dAdd of infinity and -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dAdd(nan, one)) = "NaN", "dAdd of NaN and 1")
  assert(dEQ(dSub(a, b), 3.25), "dSub")
  assert(dToString(dSub(z, z)) = "0.0", "dSub of 0.0 and 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dSub(nz, z)) = "-0.0", "dSub of -0.0 and 0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dSub(ninf, large), ninf), "dSub of -infinity and a large value")
  assert(dToString(dSub(inf, inf)) = "NaN", "dSub of infinities")
  assert(dToString(dSub(nan, one)) = "NaN", "dSub of NaN and 1")
  assert(dEQ(dMul(a, b), dNeg(1.875)), "dMul")
  assert(dEQ(dMul(a, a), 6.25), "dMul of a and a")
  assert(dToString(dMul(large, large)) = "1.0E42", "dMul of large values")
  assert(dToString(dMul(nz, a)) = "-0.0", "dMul of -0.0 and 2.5")
  assert(dEQ(dMul(inf, b), ninf), "dMul of infinity and b")
  assert(dEQ(dMul(ninf, ninf), inf), "dMul of -infinities")
  assert(dToString(dMul(inf, z)) = "NaN", "dMul of infinity and 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMul(nan, z)) = "NaN", "dMul of NaN and 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMul(nz, nz)) = "0.0", "dMul of -0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dMul(ninf, b), inf), "dMul of -infinity and b")
  assert(dEQ(dMul(ninf, a), ninf), "dMul of -infinity and a")
  assert(dToString(dMul(nan, one)) = "NaN", "dMul of NaN and 1")
  assert(dToString(dDiv(a, b)) = "-3.3333333333333335", "dDiv")
  assert(dToString(dDiv(one, ninf)) = "-0.0", "dDiv of 1 and -infinity")
  assert(dEQ(dDiv(large, large), one), "dDiv of large values")
  assert(dToString(dDiv(inf, inf)) = "NaN", "dDiv of infinities")
  assert(dToString(dDiv(nz, a)) = "-0.0", "dDiv of -0.0 and a")
  assert(dEQ(dDiv(inf, a), inf), "dDiv of infinity and a")
  assert(dEQ(dDiv(ninf, b), inf), "dDiv of -infinity and b")

  assert(dToString(dDiv(nan, one)) = "NaN", "dDiv of NaN and 1")

  assert(dToString(dSqrt(nz)) = "-0.0", "dSqrt of -0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dSqrt(inf), inf), "dSqrt of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dSqrt(b)) = "NaN", "dSqrt of a negative")

  assert(dToString(dSqrt(z)) = "0.0", "dSqrt of 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dSqrt(large)) = "3.1622776601683792E10", "dSqrt of a large value")
  assert(dToString(dSqrt(ninf)) = "NaN", "dSqrt of -infinity")

  assert(dEQ(dPow(two, inf), inf), "dPow of 2.0 and infinity")
  assert(dToString(dPow(b, 0.5)) = "NaN", "dPow of a negative at 0.5")
  assert(dEQ(dPow(4.0, 0.5), two), "dPow at 0.5")
  assert(dEQ(dPow(large, z), one), "dPow of a large value at 0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dPow(ninf, 3.0), ninf), "dPow of -infinity at 3.0")
  assert(dToString(dPow(large, two)) = "1.0E42", "dPow of a large value at 2.0")
  assert(dEQ(dPow(ninf, two), inf), "dPow of -infinity at 2.0")
  assert(dToString(dPow(inf, dNeg(one))) = "0.0", "dPow of infinity at -1.0")
  assert(dEQ(dPow(nan, z), one), "dPow of NaN at 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dPow(two, nan)) = "NaN", "dPow of 2.0 at NaN")
  assert(dToString(dPow(z, 2.0)) = "0.0", "dPow of 0.0 at 2.0")
  assert(dToString(dPow(nz, 3.0)) = "-0.0", "dPow of -0.0 at 3.0")
  assert(dEQ(dPow(inf, 0.5), inf), "dPow of infinity at 0.5")
  assert(dToString(dPow(nan, 2.0)) = "NaN", "dPow of NaN at 2.0")

  assert(dEQ(dSin(z), z), "dSin of 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dSin(nz)) = "-0.0", "dSin of -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dSin(3.141592653589793)) = "1.2246467991473532E-16", "dSin of pi")
  assert(dToString(dSin(inf)) = "NaN", "dSin of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dSin(nan)) = "NaN", "dSin of NaN")
  assert(dToString(dSin(large)) = "-0.6671201770718048", "dSin of a large value")
  assert(dToString(dSin(ninf)) = "NaN", "dSin of -infinity")
  assert(dEQ(dCos(z), one), "dCos of 0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dCos(nz), one), "dCos of -0.0")
  assert(dEQ(dCos(3.141592653589793), dNeg(one)), "dCos of pi")
  assert(dToString(dCos(ninf)) = "NaN", "dCos of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dCos(large)) = "0.7449501119831339", "dCos of a large value")
  assert(dToString(dCos(inf)) = "NaN", "dCos of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dCos(nan)) = "NaN", "dCos of NaN")

<!-- The probes of climb batch 25's planner (CLIMB-BATCH-25.md, section 4, "The planner's probes", holds their results): what each file here is, the tree it was measured on, and how to run it again. Written 2026-11-02 by an Opus planning worker against main at 0f27b2f5f, whose code is 25238e60c's, climb batch 24's landing. -->

# Climb batch 25's probes

The runs were in three worktrees seeded detached at `dc571c1f3` from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base25`, whose code is `25238e60c`'s, after its build, library order and walk run had ended at 00:41 UTC on 2026-11-02 and before its marker `tmp/BUILT` was written at 01:28: `/home/user/fortress-p25` (the code generator's runs, then the samples of N, D and P with the `asFloat` control), `/home/user/fortress-p25t` (the texts of R, U and A, then the order of application) and `/home/user/fortress-p25patch` (the six texts and samples together, built). Each was removed after. The base build ran nothing but `old-fortress.sh` runs, with their private caches folders in the probe worktrees. Machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` for the stages and the direct runs; two other workers shared the machine, the load from 0.3 to 5, so no time here is one to compare, and walk was not timed.

## The files

- `count.sh`: F-32's classes counted again on a built tree, made from `plan-24/probes/count.sh`: the natives probe's scripts read from `4a46fb83a`, with `plan-24/probes/remap.py` run on climb batch 24's table of its base, so that each of the 173 bindings that name a helper gets the glue class it named before it moved; then `plan-23/probes/movable.py`, then the column `now`. Writes `classified.tsv`, `movable.tsv`, `moved.tsv` and `helpers-javap.txt`; it reads the tree and builds nothing, so it was run on the base build itself.
- `classified-base.tsv`, `moved-base.tsv`: `count.sh`'s output on the base build. The first equals climb batch 24's `plan-24/probes/classified-base.tsv` binding for binding, line numbers included; the second lists the 173 bindings that name helpers, each with the glue class it named before it moved. Rungs A and U change six `asFloat` headers, from `Float` to `RR64`, so the next planner's `remap.py`, which matches by file, owner and header, must match those six by file and line, which their one-line edits keep.
- `n3.py` and `n3-base.tsv`: N3's 158, the class C bindings of `classified.tsv`, one line a binding with its line, owner, header, glue class, the batch's rung or the home of what it waits on, the helper's Java signature, the types the compiled checker reads it at in walk's world, whether microGPT's lines reach it, and the glue class's computation read from `interpreter/glue/prim/`. Its last lines, on standard error, count each rung.
- `codegen.sh` and `cgkinds.py`: the code generator over the distance stage's fourteen components, declaration by declaration, on the tree at `$FORTRESS_HOME`: the distance stage's shadows and driver (`tools/distance/`) with `-order full` and the flags of the probe of 2026-10-23 (`perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, section 1), whose own scripts were not kept. `cgkinds.py` counts each refused declaration once, at its first wall, by component and by the code generator's message. About 140 s on the base, 210 s with the helper strings on glue classes.
- `apply25.py`: writes a rung's text, or the planner's sample of one, into a tree at the base, by exact text, each edit matching once: `R`, `U` and `A` the whole texts; `N`, `D` and `P` the samples; `asfloat-control` `Int`'s `asFloat` moved at its header `Float`.
- `rung-R.patch`, `rung-U.patch`, `rung-A.patch`: `apply25.py`'s three texts on a clean checkout of the base, taken with `git diff`. `sample-D.patch`, `sample-P.patch`, `sample-N.patch`: its three samples, likewise. Each applies to the base alone (`git apply --check`), and the six one after another in the gather's order D, P, A, R, U, N through `git apply --3way`.

## How to run them again

From a worktree seeded from a base build at the batch's base, set up as the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md` says:

    explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/count.sh $PWD tmp/count
    python3 -B explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/n3.py tmp/count/classified.tsv ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim > tmp/n3.tsv
    explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/codegen.sh tmp/cg                     # in the background; prints the table
    python3 -B explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/apply25.py $PWD R U A      # or: git apply --3way the patches in the gather's order
    ant compileAll        # then the library order, before a compiled test
    explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/distance.txt tmp/distance        # in the background
    explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/count.txt tmp/count-scratch # in the background
    ant testSystem; ant testSpecData                                                   # in the background

The control of the code generator's run puts the 173 helper strings back on their glue classes for one run, from `tmp/count/moved.tsv` (`glue_before`, `helper_now`), the string searched from the header's line through three lines after it, since a header can span two lines. The `asFloat` control is `apply25.py <tree> asfloat-control` with the distance stage after it.

The value probes were scratch programs, not kept, each run on the old code (`tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base25 <tree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss`) and on the text (`bin/fortress P.fss`), their outputs compared with `diff`: `ValR`, R's ten at the bounds and at pairs of signs; `ValU`, `UnsignedLong`'s getters and `NN64`'s prefix `DOTMINUS` at seven values, and `NN32`'s `CHOOSE` at 128 pairs, each overflow caught; `ValA`, the six `asFloat`s at their bounds; `ValN`, `ValD` and `ValQ`, the samples of N, D and P; `ZeroZZ32`, `ZeroZZ64`, `ZeroNN32`, `ZeroNN64` and `ZeroZZ`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero in a `try` catching `DivisionByZero`. Each was a do-block of typed bindings and `println` lines, written by a script: a list literal at a declared `List[\ZZ32\]` is an `ArrayList[\Int\]` under walk and does not bind (row 364's kind), so the lists were left out. The compiled sample, `SampleRUACompiled` and `SampleNDQCompiled`, each with a `.test` of `link`, `run` and `run_out_contains=PASS`, ran through `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh samples ProjectFortress/compiler_tests SampleRUACompiled.test SampleNDQCompiled.test` after the library order on the combined tree, and on the old code through `old-fortress.sh <base build> <caches> junit <the two .test files>`; the compiled prelude's `assert` has no form over two `ZZ64` values, so those comparisons are `assert(a = b, message)`.

content.content:
# The gate

The gate runs the seven steps below on one tree, in about 25 minutes. It is green if every step passes, and red if one fails. If a step fails, run the rest, so that the summary holds every step's result.

## What it writes

The summary, `summary.txt`, has one tab-separated row for each suite: `track/suite`, tests, failures, errors, skipped. Below the rows, lines that start with `#` give each log's `BUILD` and `Total time:` lines, the machine that ran the gate (`# machine`), the atomic runs and the ladder's comparison. A landed summary can also end with `# microgpt-walk` lines: the `VERDICT:` and `rc=` lines of the microGPT walk check (`interpreter.md`, "The model program"), run on the landed tree. Add them only if your brief asks for the microGPT walk check on the landed tree.

If your brief asks you to land a gate's results, put them in a new `gate/` folder in `explorations/compile-ladder/`, under the `climb-batch-` name that your brief gives, in the form of the newest one: `summary.txt`, and in `ladder/` the files `ladder.tsv`, `microgpt-phase.md`, `comparison.txt` and `microgpt-comparison.txt`. The next gate compares with the newest summary there or in `explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/`, and finds no other. Land them in a commit that changes nothing else that the gate reads.

Steps 5 and 7 use shell functions that `explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh` defines. The file runs nothing. In each Bash call of steps 5 and 7, set up the call as `build-and-caches.md` says, which sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the tree's root. Then source the file, from the root:

    source explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh

## When to run it

Your brief says whether you run the gate. If it does not ask, run only your own tests (`tests-running.md`).

If it asks, first check whether the newest gate still holds for your tree. A gate's tables stay valid until the tree changes under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`, or in `build.xml`, outside the test files. A test file is a `.fss`, `.fsi` or `.test` file directly in `ProjectFortress/tests/` or a `ProjectFortress/*_tests/` directory. The commit that landed the newest summary changed nothing that the gate reads. Commit your tree, then run this command. It prints each path, test files excepted, changed since that commit:

    G=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt')
    git diff --name-only $G HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml \
        | grep -v -E '^ProjectFortress/([^/]*_)?tests/[^/]*\.(fss|fsi|test)$'

- If it prints a path, run the gate.
- If not, the newest gate holds. Run only the changed test files, through `harness-one.sh` and `junit.sh` (`tests-running.md`).

## The steps

Run these steps from the tree's root. Keep the logs of steps 2 and 4 in `tmp/gate/`, as `compileAll.txt`, `testFast.txt`, `testSystem.txt` and `testSpecData.txt`.

1. Read the Avail column of `df -h /`. Warning: deleting `/tmp/fortress*rats` can break other live runs. If the column shows less than 1 GB, delete `/tmp/fortress*rats`, `ProjectFortress/test-tmp` and `ProjectFortress/test-caches`, and read it again. If it still shows less than 500 MB, stop and report.
2. Run `rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS tmp/gate && mkdir -p tmp/gate`, then `ant compileAll`.
3. If the build printed `Caches <tree>/default_repository/caches started again, empty`, run the library order (`build-and-caches.md`). If not, and a source of the compiler's library changed since the caches were filled, take its step in `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library". Then copy the caches twice for the ladder regression, before anything else compiles into them:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; mkdir -p $D/root
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/ladder-caches
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/pristine

4. Run `ant testFast`, then `ant testSystem`, then `ant testSpecData`. All three must have zero failures.
5. Write the summary: `gate_summary tmp/gate tmp/gate/summary.txt`. Compare it: `gate_compare "$(last_landed_summary)" tmp/gate/summary.txt`. It prints a line for a suite with failures or errors, a suite with no tests, a suite whose count of tests fell, and a suite that is gone. Each such line makes the gate red. A count that rose prints nothing.
6. Do the atomic runs, and append their lines to the summary.
7. Do the ladder regression.

## The atomic runs

The atomic runs compile fourteen programs, and run each one three times at four threads, in about a minute. They need the library's jars in the tree's caches (`build-and-caches.md`). Run them from `ProjectFortress/`:

    for p in AtomicTopLevelObjectVar AtomicTopLevelVar MutableTopLevelVarInLoop FirstLoadThreadsRungG \
             atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 \
             nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2 ; do
      d=other_compiler_tests ; [ -f compiler_tests/$p.fss ] && d=compiler_tests
      timeout -k 5 300 ../bin/fortress compile $d/$p.fss >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "# atomic $p COMPILE-FAILED" ; continue ; }
      for i in 1 2 3 ; do
        out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$?
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && { out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$? ; }
        case "$out" in *FAIL*) r=FAIL ;; *PASS*) r=PASS ;; *) r="NO-PASS rc=$rc" ;; esac
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && r=TIMEOUT-TWICE
        echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 $r"
      done
    done

The gate is red on any FAIL, NO-PASS, COMPILE-FAILED or TIMEOUT-TWICE.

## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

## Comparing with an earlier run

- `ant testSystem` runs in four shards, the summary's rows `system-0` to `system-3`. A shard takes the files by their place in a sorted list, so an added file moves every later file to another shard. When you compare by hand, compare only the sum of the four. `gate_compare` sums them.
- In printed output, mask only these differences: the `Operation took <n>ms` line, a Java line number in a stack frame, an object's identity hash (`@` and hex digits), and a position in a library file that your change moved. In your report, list each test with a masked difference, and the kinds masked in it.
- If your brief asks you to compare the interpreter tests with a base run, use the two scripts in `explorations/coordinator/tools/count-run/`. `count-run.sh` runs every `ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss` under walk, one JVM per test: run it once on the base commit and once after your edit. `compare-normalised.py` compares the two runs, with the last three masks above. Each script's header gives its usage.

component testRR32

run():() = do

  v : RR32 = narrow(4.5)

  zero : RR32 = narrow(0.0)
  one : RR32 = narrow(1.0)
  two : RR32 = narrow(2.0)
  four : RR32 = narrow(4.0)
  five : RR32 = narrow(5.0)
  nfour : RR32 = narrow(-4.0)
  nfive : RR32 = narrow(-5.0)
  infinity: RR32 = narrow(1.0) / narrow(0.0)
  NaN: RR32 = infinity - infinity

  assert(x = y)
  assert(x =/= z)
  assert(x < z)
  assert(x <= z)
  assert(z > x)
  assert(z >= x)
  assert(x CMP z, LessThan)
  assert(x MIN z, x)
  assert(x MAX z, z)
  assert((x MIN NaN).isNaN, true)
  assert((x MAX NaN).isNaN, true)
  assert(-x, narrow(-14.0))
  assert(x + y, sum)
  assert(x - y, zero)
  assert(x DOT y, z)
  assert(x TIMES y, z)
  assert(z, mul)
  assert(z / x, x)

  assert(SQRT z, x)
  assert(x PLUS_UP y, sum)
  assert(x MINUS_UP y, zero)
  assert(x DOT_UP y, mul)
  assert(x SLASH_UP y, one)
  assert(SQRT_UP z, x)
  assert(x PLUS_DOWN y, sum)
  assert(x MINUS_DOWN y, zero)
  assert(x DOT_DOWN y, mul)
  assert(x SLASH_DOWN y, one)
  assert(SQRT_DOWN z, x)
  assert(|x|, x)
  assert(|-x|, x)
  assert(x^two, mul)
  assert(floor v, four)
  assert(|\ v /|, four)
  assert(ceiling v, five)
  assert(|/ v \|, five)
  assert(truncate v, four)
  assert(floor w, nfive)
  assert(|\ w /|, nfive)
  assert(ceiling w, nfour)
  assert(|/ w \|, nfour)
  assert(truncate w, nfour)
  assert(x.isNaN, false)
  assert(x.isInfinite, false)
  assert(infinity.isInfinite, true)
  assert(x.isNumber, true)
  assert(x.isFinite, true)
  assert(infinity.isFinite, false)
  assert(Just(v), Just(v))
  assert(Just(z), Just(z))
  (* If we do not give explicit type instantiation below, it fails... *)
  assert(x.check, Just[\RR32\](x))
  assert(infinity.check, Nothing[\RR32\])
  assert(NaN.check, Nothing[\RR32\])

  assert(x.check_star, Just[\RR32\](x))
  assert(infinity.check_star, Just[\RR32\](infinity))
  assert(NaN.check_star, Nothing[\RR32\])

  (* We want to implement hexadecimal literals. *)
  assert((x / x).rawBits, 1065353216)
  assert(x MINNUM z, x)
  assert(x MAXNUM z, z)
  assert(x MINNUM NaN, x)
  assert(x MAXNUM NaN, x)
end

end

and \EXP{/} is subtle.
\See{operator-precedence} for a discussion of the relative precedence of
these operations and how precedence may depend on the use of whitespace.

The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
Rational computations do not overflow.
For floating-point results, overflow produces \EXP{+\infty} or \EXP{-\infty}
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, overflow produces an appropriate containing interval.

Underflow is relevant only to floating-point computations and is handled
according to the rules of IEEE 754.

The handling of division by zero depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, division by zero throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}.
For rational results, division by zero produces \EXP{1/0}.
For floating-point results, division by zero produces a \TYP{NaN} value
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, division by zero produces an appropriate containing interval
(which under many circumstances will be the interval of all possible real values and infinities).

Wraparound multiplication on fixed-size integers is expressed by
\EXP{\dottimes}.
Saturating multiplication on fixed-size integers is expressed by
\EXP{\boxdot} or \EXP{\boxtimes}.
These operations do not overflow.

Ordinary multiplication and division of floating-point numbers always
use the IEEE 754 ``round to nearest'' rounding mode.  This rounding
mode may be emphasized by using the operators \EXP{\otimes} (or \EXP{\odot})
and \EXP{\oslash}.  Multiplication and division in ``round toward zero''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\boxtimes} (or \EXP{\boxdot}) and
\EXP{\boxslash}.
Multiplication and division in ``round toward positive infinity''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\uptimes} (or \EXP{\updot}) and \EXP{\upslash}.
Multiplication and division in ``round toward negative infinity''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\downtimes} (or \EXP{\downdot}) and
\EXP{\downslash}.

\subsection{Addition and Subtraction Operators}

Addition and subtraction are expressed with \EXP{+} and \EXP{-} on all numeric quantities,
including intervals, as well as vectors and matrices.

The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
Rational computations do not overflow.
For floating-point results, overflow produces \EXP{+\infty} or \EXP{-\infty}
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, overflow produces an appropriate containing interval.

Underflow is relevant only to floating-point computations and is handled
according to the rules of IEEE 754.

Wraparound addition and subtraction on fixed-size integers are
expressed by \EXP{\dotplus} and \EXP{\dotminus}.
Saturating addition and subtraction on fixed-size integers are
expressed by \EXP{\boxplus} and \EXP{\boxminus}.
These operations do not overflow.

Ordinary addition and subtraction of floating-point numbers always
use the IEEE 754 ``round to nearest'' rounding mode.  This rounding
mode may be emphasized by using the operators \EXP{\oplus}
and \EXP{\ominus}.  Addition and subtraction in ``round toward zero''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\boxplus} and \EXP{\boxminus}.
Addition and subtraction in ``round toward positive infinity''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\upplus} and \EXP{\upminus}.
Addition and subtraction in ``round toward negative infinity''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\downplus} and \EXP{\downminus}.

The construction \EXP{x \pm y} produces the interval \EXP{\bsINT{x-y,x+y}}.

content.content:
## B.12 Native code and Java interop

The two worlds bind native code by two mechanisms that share nothing but the word "native".

Interpreter: a function whose body is literally `builtinPrimitive("some.java.Class")` is pattern-matched in `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative` (`interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-229`). A string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` names a static Java method, `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.Class.method"`: `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` takes, among the class's public static methods of that name, the one whose Java types carry the declared types, `self` first, and calls it by reflection, each argument unboxed and the result boxed (`NativeApp.java:200-207`; since rung W, `640acb4a1`; F-299). Any other string names a class — a subclass of `NativeFn0..3`/`NativeMeth0..3` in `interpreter/glue/` — which is loaded reflectively and takes the evaluator's boxed `FValue`s directly.

There are 231 such bindings in `LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, 108 in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and 7 in `LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss`.

Compiler: a `.fss` writes `import java com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.{class.method => name, …}` (16 such lines in `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`, 3 in `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`); `ForeignJava` reads the Java class with ASM to synthesize an api for it (`repository/ForeignJava.java:132-136,565-575`), and `FortressTransformer` rewrites the class into a wrapper whose methods take and return the compiled world's boxed values (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressTransformer.java:37`, wrapper written to `nativewrapper_cache` at `:33`).

`import java` also works on the interpreter path, by a third route that is easy to miss: `ForeignComponentWrapper` populates an environment from `ForeignJava`'s synthesized declarations (`interpreter/env/ForeignComponentWrapper.java:59`), and `ClosureMaker` generates, at run time, a `NativeFn<n>` subclass that calls the Java method and writes it into `bytecode_cache` (`interpreter/env/ClosureMaker.java:44-50,52`).

No test under `ProjectFortress/tests/` uses `import java` (0 files), while 2 under `compiler_tests/` do, so the interpreter's foreign-Java route is present but not exercised by the gated suite.

There is no way for a Fortress program to be called *from* Java other than by loading the generated classes through `InstantiatingClassloader`, which is what `MainWrapper` does.

4426:\subsection{A native binding that names a static helper}
\item[Effect] 173 of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper:
the operators \EXP{=}, \EXP{<}, the prefix and infix \EXP{-} and
\EXP{\dotminus}, \EXP{+}, \EXP{\dotplus}, \EXP{\cdot}, \EXP{\times},
juxtaposition, \EXP{\dottimes}, \EXP{\div}, \OPR{BITAND}, \OPR{BITOR},
\OPR{BITXOR}, \OPR{BITNOT} and \OPR{CHOOSE} of the traits \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}
and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, with the functions \VAR{widen} and \VAR{unsigned} of
the first and \VAR{narrow}, \VAR{unsigned} and \VAR{big} of the second, and the
same operators but \EXP{<} and \OPR{CHOOSE} of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}};
eighteen bindings of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and of the interpreter's
objects twenty-one of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, forty of \TYP{Char} and thirty of
\TYP{Float}; the getters \VAR{asString} and \VAR{asExprString} of the
interpreter's objects \TYP{Int}, \TYP{Long} and \TYP{BigNum}; and the function
\VAR{char}.
The other 276 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call.
Until the compiled code moves onto \library, the type checker checks the moved
bindings, but no compiled program runs them.
Where a binding declares \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} or \TYP{Char}
at a position at which its helper takes or answers a Java \texttt{int} or
\texttt{long}, the compiler composes the call with one of six transfer helpers
at that position, as the compiled library writes its own operations on those
types, and the type checker checks the composition.
Under the interpreter a helper's raise of \TYP{IntegerOverflow} or
\TYP{DivisionByZero} is the library's own exception, so \EXP{\div} by zero on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}
and \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}, as \chapref{operators}
says of an integer result; \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD}, which still name glue
classes, end the run with a Java exception at a divisor of zero, on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} (row~336 of the revival's gap
ledger) and on \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}
(row~848 of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter passes a helper declared over \TYP{String}, as its glue classes
do, the name of the value's type in place of its characters where the value is
not a flat string, as a \TYP{String} made by concatenating two long strings
(row~846 of the revival's gap ledger).
For a method, the interpreter is told the type that declares it: it refuses at
load a helper bound in a method of a type that no Java type carries, as a
program's own object, and takes only an overload whose first Java parameter
carries that type, which it reads by the type's name, for the types of
\library\ whose names no program can give its own types.
It refuses such a binding in a dotted method of a generic trait or object only
where an instance's method is made, so a program that makes no instance loads
(row~864 of the revival's gap ledger); and it reads the declaring type, not the
value's, so a program's object that extends a carried trait of \library\
against its \KWD{comprises} clause, which the interpreter loads (row~551 of the
revival's gap ledger), still reaches the helper with a value that no Java type
carries.
The compiler leaves a declaration with a varargs parameter as a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, so the type checker does not check such a binding
against its helper (row~849 of the revival's gap ledger); no binding of
\library\ that names a helper has a varargs parameter.
Nor does it rewrite such a body in a local function or in a method of an object
expression, which stays a call of \VAR{builtinPrimitive} and does not compile
(row~865 of the revival's gap ledger); \library\ has no binding in either.

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the raw compile/run outputs of run-ladder.sh into the ladder table.

Reads  explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv  and  raw/<corpus>/<file>.{compile,run}
Writes explorations/compile-ladder/ladder.tsv    (one row per file, diffable)
       explorations/compile-ladder/summary.txt   (the counts and the rankings)

Phase vocabulary, and where each decision comes from:

content.content:
== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

## What changed and why

- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:51`, `javaFor`: `if (t.equals("RR64") || t.equals("Float")) return double.class;`. content.content:
\subsection{A native binding that names a static helper}
\seclabel{revival-native-helpers}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{FortressBuiltin}: the comment of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive} in the \apiN\ \TYP{FortressBuiltin}, which this
specification typesets from the \apiN's source file.
\item[Change] The comment says that the argument of \VAR{builtinPrimitive}
names either a glue class, a subclass of
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp}, which only the
interpreter runs, or a helper, a public static method of a Java class of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, which both the interpreter
and the compiled code call; that the interpreter loads a helper beside its glue
classes, taking among the methods of that name the one whose Java parameter and
result types carry the declared types, \KWD{self} first, and carrying each value
at its declared type; that the compiler, before type checking, rewrites such a
body into a call of the helper, which the type checker checks against the
helper's Java signature; and that a string under that package that names no
such method is an error on both.
It also names the package that defines the subclasses of the classes
\texttt{NativeFn0} to \texttt{NativeFn4}
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim}, where it said
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.primitive}, a package that the
implementation does not have.
The comment gains a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 10~October 2026 that every native binding of \library\
keeps the library's own form, a body that is exactly a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, and that its string names a static helper of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, the compiled code's own
helpers, in place of a glue class, which takes the interpreter's values and
which the compiled code cannot call.
The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and the type checker checks each
moved binding against its helper's Java signature from the step that moves it.
The alternative not taken was \KWD{import} \KWD{java} declarations written in
the source files of \library, the compiler's own form for its natives, which
the interpreter does not run.
A reversal would restore the original comment, put the moved bindings back on
their glue classes, and leave the compiled code without a binding of the
natives of \library\ that it can call.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-natives-walk/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
(** The %builtinPrimitive% function is actually recognized as a special piece
    of built-in magic by the Fortress interpreter and, where its argument names a helper, by the compiler.  The %javaClass%
    argument names either a glue class, a Java Class which is a subclass of
    \texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp}, which provides code
    for the closure which is used in place of the call to
    %builtinPrimitive% and which only the interpreter runs, or a helper, a public static method of a Java class of the package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, written \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.}\textit{Class}\texttt{.}\textit{method}, which both the interpreter and the compiled code call.  The interpreter loads a helper beside its glue classes: among the methods of that name it takes the one whose Java parameter and result types carry the declared types, %self% first, and it carries each value at its declared type.  The compiler, before type checking, rewrites the body into a call of the helper, which the type checker checks against the helper's Java signature.  A string under \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers} that names no such method is an error on both.  Meanwhile all the necessary type information,
    argument names, etc. must be declared here in Fortress-land.  For examples, see the end of this file.
    \revision{revival-native-helpers}{The argument names a glue class, which only the interpreter runs, or a static helper of \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, which both the interpreter and the compiled code call; and the package that defines the subclasses of the %NativeFn% classes is named as the implementation names it.}

    In practice, if you are extending the interpreter you will probably
    want to extend \texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeFn0,1,2,3,4}
    or one of their subclasses defined in
    \texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim}.  These types are
    generally easier to work with, and the boilerplate packing and
    unpacking of values is done for you.
**)

content.content:
rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"
